A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, architectures and central results. Their complete text, equations, figures, table and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison after matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical constructions and complexity proofs, not original experimental, simulation or data-analysis outcomes. Its figures illustrate architectures and circuits; Table 1 compares theoretical properties.

after.justification: v2 remains theoretical, including its appendices. The added CIFAR-10 example illustrates the problem definition without reporting an experiment or measured outcome.

M1.justification: The vector-encoding operations, convolution construction, residual blocks and three QRAM regimes are retained. Added explanations and suggestions for alternative activations do not change the implemented procedures.

E1.justification: Neither version evaluates datasets or tasks empirically. v2's CIFAR-10 example and discussion of possible UNet applications do not establish additional training or evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Cong, Allcock, Kerenidis and Guo with the same architectural properties. No comparison method is added, removed or substantively revised.

E3.justification: Neither version contains an empirical evaluation protocol. The architectural settings underlying Theorem 2, including 16-channel convolutions, 3-by-3 filters, padding and stride, are unchanged.

E4.justification: No ablations, robustness tests or empirical case studies are introduced or removed. The appendix analyses of norm preservation, QRAM feasibility, receptive fields and dequantization are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The retained approximation-error bounds are theoretical guarantees, not statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Table 1's comparison entries and the reported polylogarithmic, quartic-speedup and quadratic-speedup conclusions are unchanged. Neither version contains measured performance results.

T1.justification: Definition 1 adds the explicit assumption 0 ≤ epsilon ≤ 1. Otherwise, the mathematical results and proofs are retained. v1's pooling Definition B.7 and Lemma B.20 become Definition C.1 and Lemma C.1 through relocation, without changing their substance.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion are unchanged. Both versions claim coherent multilayer neural-network inference, the same matrix-vector-squared construction and convolution encoding, and the same speedups under three data-access regimes.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly presents erf as an analytically convenient choice and identifies GELU/tanh alternatives. It adds prospects for shallow UNet diffusion models and training acceleration. Existing depth, QRAM and dequantization limitations remain.

D1.justification: The circuit constructions, QRAM data structures, preprocessing requirements and resource bounds are retained. v2's additional circuit explanations clarify existing constructions without adding implementation settings, code or data-access resources.

R1.justification: The 114 cited works and their substantive roles are retained after matching updated titles and publication records. Bibliographic corrections and author–year citations do not change the research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds localized explanations around the sampling problem, convolution encoding and architecture composition, while removing the short quantum-computing primer. It relocates pooling material and author contributions, updates citation style and makes language corrections; the overall organization remains.

P2.justification: The architecture and circuit diagrams and Table 1 retain their content. Table 1 moves from page 3 to page 4, several figures shift with text reflow, and conference headers are added. There is no substantive visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The concrete sampling example and Section 4's explanation of how existing lemmas compose into network blocks make the theoretical contribution easier to follow. Removing the brief quantum-computing primer reduces introductory context, but the added task-specific explanations support a modest net improvement. The central guarantees and supporting proofs remain essentially unchanged.
